title: Heart-rate variability falls with age: the Fantasia young-vs-elderly contrast in the frequency domain

dataset.name: Fantasia Database
dataset.record: 10 young (f1y01-10, 21-34 y) + 10 elderly (f1o01-10, 68-81 y), resting ECG @ 250 Hz; fixed 10-min window t=300-900 s
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol. 1996;271(4):R1078-84. Goldberger AL, et al. PhysioNet. Circulation. 2000;101(23):e215-20.

proposition: Frequency-domain HRV on real resting ECG recovers the textbook signature of cardiovascular aging: overall HRV power is markedly lower in the elderly than the young (median total power 1021 vs 3596 ms^2, Wilcoxon p = 0.0004) and high-frequency vagal power is lower too (p = 0.004) - while the normalised sympathovagal balance (LF/HF, HFnu) and the resting mean heart rate do NOT separate the groups.

claims.statement: HF (vagal) power young-vs-elderly Wilcoxon p (young > elderly)
LF/HF balance ratio young-vs-elderly Wilcoxon p (no separation)

validation.reference: The established physiology of cardiovascular aging - a loss of heart-rate variability, especially overall power and the high-frequency (vagal) band (Task Force of ESC/NASPE, 1996) - and the Fantasia database's own young-vs-elderly design (Iyengar et al. 1996)
validation.data: REAL - Fantasia (PhysioNet), 10 young + 10 elderly resting ECG, fixed 10-min window
validation.note: Aggregate acceptance: the two HRV-magnitude indices are significantly lower in the elderly in the expected direction - total power (young median 3596 vs 1021 ms^2, p = 0.0004) and HF vagal power (p = 0.004). Reported honestly as NOT separating the groups: the normalised balance indices LF/HF and HFnu (p = 0.66) and the resting mean heart rate (p = 0.34) - aging shows in HRV magnitude, not in the balance ratios or the mean rate. One elderly record (f1o09) was flagged for frequent ectopy by ecgHRVfreq's rhythm_check and excluded from the frequency-domain metrics (frequency HRV is undefined under ectopy), leaving 10 young vs 9 elderly for those metrics.

open_questions.q: The normalised sympathovagal indices (LF/HF, HFnu) do not distinguish the age groups here even though absolute power does - consistent with the view that normalisation removes the very magnitude collapse that carries the aging signal. Whether a longer or multi-window analysis would reveal a balance shift is a real question, but the magnitude result is the robust one and is what we claim. Documented, not escalated.
